samples.text:
The pie charts shows the market share of five video streaming services in a country in 2019 and in 2024.

In 2019, Service A was the biggest service by far, it had 52% of the market. Service B had 21% and Service C had 14%. Service D and Service E was very small with only 8% and 5%. So Service A had more than half of all the market in this year.

In 2024, Service A was still the most popular but its share fell down to 34%. Service B also decreased a little to 19%. On the other hand, the other three services grew. Service D increased very much to 17%, it is more than double. Service E also increased from 5% to 14% and Service C went up slightly to 16%.

Overall, Service A lost a lot of customers but it was still number one. The smaller services become more strong, so in 2024 the market was more equal between the services than in 2019.
samples.why: All key figures included accurately · overview present but placed last and slightly imprecise (customers vs share) · repetitive linking · adequate vocabulary · several agreement, word-form and punctuation errors.

samples.text:
The pie charts compare the market shares held by five video streaming services in one country in 2019 and 2024.

Overall, Service A remained the market leader in both years, but its dominance declined significantly. At the same time, the smaller services, particularly D and E, grew considerably, so that the market became much more evenly divided.

In 2019, Service A controlled just over half of the market (52%). Service B was a distant second, with 21%, followed by Service C at 14%. Services D and E had only small shares, at 8% and 5% respectively.

By 2024, Service A's share had fallen to 34%, a drop of 18 percentage points. Service B also lost ground slightly, falling to 19%. In contrast, Service D more than doubled its share to 17%, overtaking Service C, which rose modestly to 16%. The most rapid growth was seen in Service E, which almost trebled its share from 5% to 14%. As a result, the gap between the largest and smallest services narrowed considerably over the five-year period.
samples.why: Clear overview of the key trend · main changes highlighted with accurate figures and correct derived values · logical progression · range of linkers · good collocations (market leader, lost ground) · few errors.

samples.text:
The charts show how the market for video streaming in one country was shared among five services in 2019 and 2024.

The market became noticeably more competitive over the five years: Service A retained the largest share but lost much of its dominance, while the smaller providers, especially Services D and E, made substantial gains.

In 2019, Service A was unrivalled, with 52% of the market, more than double the share of its nearest competitor, Service B (21%). Service C held 14%, and Services D and E were marginal players, with 8% and 5% respectively.

By 2024, Service A's share had shrunk to 34%, and although it was still the leader, it no longer accounted for even half of the market. Service B slipped slightly to 19%, whereas Service C edged up to 16%. The most striking gains were made by the two smallest services: Service D more than doubled its share to 17%, overtaking Service C, and Service E nearly trebled its share to 14%. Consequently, the four challengers together held around two-thirds of the market by 2024, compared with less than half five years earlier.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected with a clear overview · figures used selectively for comparison with accurate derived values · cohesion managed smoothly · precise vocabulary (unrivalled, marginal players) · wide range of error-free structures.
